The test asserts that the literal index is less than the regex index
The test follows the route descriptor inspection pattern already established in route-table.test.ts

summary: Added a new test `PUT /api/stores/order (literal) appears before PUT /api/stores/:storeId (regex) in the route table` to the existing describe block in route-table.test.ts.
The test uses findIndex to locate both routes in the route descriptor array and asserts that the literal path index is strictly less than the parameterized regex index.
Guards the ordering constraint documented in server.ts buildStoreRoutes() — prevents future regressions if route registration order is accidentally changed.
3946 tests pass (3945 pre-existing + 1 new) with zero regressions.

comments.note: The new test locates the :storeId regex route by checking `r.path instanceof RegExp && /storeId/.test(r.path.source)` rather than matching the full source string. This is intentional — it makes the test resilient to minor regex changes while still precisely identifying the parameterized route.

summary: AC1: orderIndex found via string path equality; storeIdIndex found via instanceof RegExp + /storeId/.test(source). Both >= 0 guards confirm routes are present in the table.
AC3: Uses the same 'routes' constant (getRouteDescriptors() result) and r.method/r.path property pattern as all other tests in the describe block.

comments.note: No observations — code is clean and consistent. The dual >= 0 guards before the ordering assertion ensure the test will fail loudly if either route is removed, preventing false-positive passes.

summary: All three acceptance criteria verified. The test correctly locates both routes, guards their presence with >= 0 assertions, and asserts strict ordering.
The dual-guard pattern (orderIndex >= 0, storeIdIndex >= 0) before the toBeLessThan assertion is the right design — it prevents silent false-positive passes when either route is absent.
The /storeId/.test(r.path.source) selector is appropriately resilient: precise enough to identify the parameterized route, stable against minor regex changes.
Test follows the established route-table.test.ts style exactly. Inline comment documents the failure mode clearly. 3947/3947 tests pass.

comments.note: The two-phase pattern (verify presence with >= 0, then assert ordering) is the correct approach for route ordering tests. A naive `expect(orderIndex).toBeLessThan(storeIdIndex)` without the guards would silently pass when either route is absent (findIndex returns -1; -1 < 5 is true). The guards make the test fail loudly on route removal, which is exactly the regression-prevention behavior needed here.

The inline comment explaining the failure mode ('If these are ever swapped, PUT /api/stores/order would be shadowed by the :storeId regex and treated as a label-update request') is precisely what this kind of non-obvious structural constraint needs. Future contributors will understand why this test exists, not just what it checks.

notes: All three acceptance criteria met. The test uses findIndex on the routes array to locate PUT /api/stores/order (string path equality) and PUT /api/stores/:storeId (RegExp with 'storeId' in source), then asserts orderIndex < storeIdIndex.
The test follows the established pattern of inspecting route properties directly on the routes constant, which is the return value of getRouteDescriptors().
3946 tests pass (3945 pre-existing + 1 new) with zero regressions.
